subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What are the main types of concerns patients come in with in these visit notes?

judge.implied_focus: The nature/type of the patient's presenting clinical concern in each visit

per_column.name: concern_type
per_column.rationale: Directly categorises the kind of clinical concern (acute, chronic, routine, preventive, etc.), which is the core of the query about types of concerns patients present with.

per_column.name: clinical_domain
per_column.rationale: Specifies the medical specialty/body-system context of the concern, a coherent facet that differentiates concern types by clinical area rather than restating concern_type.

per_column.name: visit_stage_in_continuum
per_column.rationale: Locates the concern along the care continuum (new presentation, follow-up, exacerbation, screening), adding a temporal/care-stage facet that meaningfully qualifies the concern without duplicating the others.

judge.rationale: All three columns centre on one coherent, data-inferable focus: characterising the patient's presenting concern. concern_type supplies the primary typology directly answering the query, while clinical_domain and visit_stage_in_continuum form complementary, non-redundant facets (clinical area and position in the care continuum) at a useful granularity. There is minor conceptual overlap between the acute/chronic/follow-up values of concern_type and visit_stage_in_continuum, which slightly weakens differentiation, but they are distinct enough to constitute a sound analytical structure rather than a restatement. The implied focus is clearly actionable: an analyst can profile and segment the dominant concern types (e.g., the large acute_diagnosis share) across domains and care stages to investigate demand patterns. This is not a mechanical/generic set, so the claim is well realised.
